body:
O3 MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. I offered a number that would refute me; here it is, and it does not.

WOG source view, 84 nodes, world order known. Discourse distance |discoursePosition(a) -
discoursePosition(b)| for every edge in every relation layer:

  layer                edges  adjacent(<=1)   max   mean
  DiscourseSuccession     80             80     1   1.00
  WorldTime               35             21    12   2.09
  Causal                   9              4    45   9.22
  EntityContinuity       688             78    70   8.54
  Hierarchy               83              6    62  26.31
  Goal                     3              1    21  13.00
  StateChange              4              2     7   3.25
  Reference               11              1    31  15.91

DiscourseSuccession is adjacent 80/80 with max 1 - it IS the rail, which is the control that says the
measurement is reading the right coordinate. EVERY OTHER LAYER IS NOT LOCAL. Causal edges reach 45
positions on an 84-node view, more than half the document. EntityContinuity is the largest layer at
688 edges and only 11% of them are adjacent. Hierarchy averages 26 positions.

So the spike's question - "are these overwhelmingly local, such that portals alone suffice?" -
answers NO on the only real source we have. There is no page size that makes a 45-position causal
edge fit on a page with its partner.

AND THE CLOCKS ACTUALLY DIVERGE, which is the part that matters for the science rather than the
layout:

  ordered node pairs             3782
  world-time and discourse ORDER DISAGREE   372   (9.8%)

That is not a hypothetical. One pair in ten is narrated in the opposite order from which it happened
in the story world. vision.md's second research question is whether recall followed presentation
order or story-world time; on WOG those two orders differ on ~10% of pairs, so A SINGLE FUSED VIEW
WOULD DESTROY THE ONLY SIGNAL THAT QUESTION IS ASKED OF. The second view is not a rendering
concession - it is where that 9.8% becomes visible.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and I would rather say it than let the table carry more weight than it
holds:
  - ONE SOURCE. WOG is 84 nodes of folk narrative with heavy flashback structure; a linear news
    report would likely show far less divergence. n=1 on sources is the same problem as n=2 on
    recall units, one level up.
  - DISTANCES ARE IN NODE INDEX, NOT PAGES. Whether an edge crosses a page depends on pagination we
    have not chosen. What the numbers show is that the edges are long relative to the document, not
    that any particular fold is crossed.
  - I did not measure how many relations a reader would need SIMULTANEOUSLY, which is the actual
    usability question and is not answerable from the graph.

The probe is a scratch file and is not committed. If the epic wants this as a slice artifact rather
than a board post, say so and I will make it a proper fixture assertion with the numbers pinned - it
is about fifteen lines and it would then fail loudly if a future source view changed shape.
